project.name: efficiency-memo
project.description: EfficiencyMemo is a pnpm monorepo that hosts a unified tool gallery behind a single Next.js shell with Supabase authentication, currently shipping Charger-Reminder for battery tracking and CoreHour for time tracking. The shell discovers new productivity tools at build time through a dynamic feature registry under apps/web/src/features. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the top-level docs to understand what EfficiencyMemo is: a pnpm monorepo wrapping a Supabase-authenticated Next.js 16 shell that hosts independent productivity tools. README gives the elevator pitch and quick-start, ARCHITECTURE.md walks the App Router route groups, auth flow, and tool-registry mechanism, and the root AGENTS.md captures the conventions every contributor (human or AI) must follow. Together they set the vocabulary for the rest of the tour.

tour.title: Monorepo Structure
tour.description: The root configuration files declare the monorepo's three workspace members (apps/web, packages/shared, packages/ui) and the shared dev/test/lint scripts. pnpm-workspace.yaml is the source of truth for which folders pnpm treats as packages, and tsconfig.base.json enforces strict mode across the whole tree. Everything in Steps 3-10 depends on this layout.

tour.title: Next.js App Shell
tour.description: The deployable surface is a Next.js 16 App Router app. The root layout wraps the entire tree, the (auth) route group hosts the magic-link sign-in flow, and the (shell) route group renders the authenticated sidebar layout after enforcing a session. HomePage redirects to the dashboard or sign-in, the dashboard lists every registered tool as a card, and ShellLayoutClient wires the sidebar, mobile drawer, and sign-out form together.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router route groups — (auth) and (shell) — let the same URL tree host different layouts without affecting the URL; the parenthesised name is a layout boundary, not a path segment.

tour.title: Tool Registry Mechanism
tour.description: The self-registration system is what lets new tools drop into the shell without editing the dashboard. registry.ts keeps a Map of manifests keyed by id, types.ts defines the ToolManifest and ComponentLoader contracts, discovery.ts walks the features directory and wires up loaders, routes.ts converts manifests into Next.js dynamic-route paths, and the [toolId]/page.tsx catch-all resolves a URL to a manifest, dynamically imports the tool's component, and falls back to notFound() for unknown ids.
tour.languageLesson: Module side-effect imports — each tool's index.ts calls registerTool at the top level so that simply importing the file wires it into the in-memory registry, no central config required.

tour.title: Feature Tool Pattern
tour.description: Every tool follows the same three-file pattern under apps/web/src/features/<tool-id>/. manifest.ts exports a ToolManifest with id, label, accent, and route template; component-loader.ts returns a dynamic import for the tool's primary page; index.ts is the side-effect entry that calls registerTool at import time. Both Charger-Reminder and CoreHour use this exact contract — adding a third tool means dropping in a new folder and one index import.

tour.title: Charger-Reminder Deep-Dive
tour.description: Charger-Reminder tracks battery-powered devices and computes when to remind the user to charge them. contracts.ts is the single source of truth for the device/charge-event/reminder-state domain types, devices.ts is the server-side data-access layer that routes between Supabase and a mock store for E2E, heuristic-engine.ts runs the deterministic v1 reminder algorithm, and the components (device-form, device-detail, device-card, device-list) compose the UI consumed by the (shell)/tools/charger-reminder pages.
tour.languageLesson: The deterministic heuristic engine is a pure function: same inputs always produce the same reminder state, which is why the unit tests can lock snapshots without mocking the clock or database.

tour.title: CoreHour Deep-Dive
tour.description: CoreHour is a time-tracking tool with periodic check-ins and tag-based categorisation. types.ts declares the Session, Tag, CheckIn, and SessionTag contracts, server-actions.ts is the sole data-mutation surface (start/end sessions, CRUD tags, submit check-ins, read/write settings), the hooks layer (context.tsx plus use-timer.ts and use-history.ts) exposes a ref-stable provider API to components, and the dashboard plus session-controller orchestrate the timer, the check-in modal, and the tag bar.
tour.languageLesson: useTimer uses a visibility-change listener to auto-pause when the tab is hidden, mirroring the behaviour of a desktop timer app without relying on background workers.

tour.title: Shared Library
tour.description: @memo/shared is the dependency-free leaf package that every other tool and the shell import. types.ts declares the cross-tool contracts (ToolManifest, ToolRegistration, User, DashboardTool) that tie the registry, the shell sidebar, and the per-tool features together; constants.ts exposes the three app-wide runtime values (APP_NAME, APP_DESCRIPTION, DEFAULT_REDIRECT); and the package's AGENTS.md documents the cycle-free, no-runtime-deps constraint that keeps it stable.

tour.title: UI Library
tour.description: @memo/ui is the React + Tailwind v4 component primitive library that both the shell and the feature tools compose. The barrel index.ts re-exports the public surface; Shell, Sidebar, Button, Card, and Modal cover the recurring patterns (responsive layout, collapsible nav, polymorphic button, tappable card, accessible dialog). No tool implements its own button or card — they reach for these primitives, which is what keeps the design consistent as new tools land.

tour.title: Data Schema
tour.description: Three Supabase Postgres migrations define every table the app reads or writes. The Charger-Reminder migration creates five cr_-prefixed tables (presets, devices, charge events, reminder preferences, computed reminder states) with FKs to auth.users; the seed migration populates the default device-type presets; and the CoreHour migration creates five ch_-prefixed tables (tags, sessions, check-ins, check-in entries, settings) converted from SQLite. All table names are tool-prefixed so additional tools can land without colliding with existing schemas.
tour.languageLesson: Tool-prefixed table names (cr_, ch_) give the project room to add new tools without coordination overhead — every new tool picks its own two-letter namespace and ships its own migration file under supabase/migrations/.

tour.title: Configuration and Deployment
tour.description: The configuration files encode how the app builds, lints, tests, and deploys. apps/web/package.json pins Next.js 16, React 19, and the @supabase/ssr dependency and exposes the dev/build/test/test:e2e/typecheck scripts. apps/web/tsconfig.json wires the @/* and @memo/* path aliases, vercel.json drives the deployment, and the PostCSS, ESLint, and Next config files keep the build pipeline predictable.

tour.title: Testing, Mock Auth, and End-to-End
tour.description: The test strategy is layered: Vitest + Testing Library for components, hooks, and the deterministic Charger-Reminder heuristic; pg-mem for SQL integration tests against the real migration files; and Playwright for end-to-end flows. The mock-auth path is what makes the E2E suite deterministic — the locked efficiency-memo-mock-auth cookie is set by the bypass API route and the mockBypassAction, recognised by getSessionUser as a valid user without hitting Supabase, and used by the charger-reminder, cross-tool, and tool-registry specs.
tour.languageLesson: Mock auth is the only contract the project locks for E2E: the cookie name, env flag, and email normaliser are all imported through the same helpers so unit tests, integration tests, and Playwright specs all agree on what a 'signed-in user' looks like.
